contributions.statement: Add static taint rules (CodeQL/Semgrep) to in-house MCP servers that treat tool return values, exception messages and log calls as sinks for secrets and personal data, and scan third-party servers before adoption, since more than 10% of 10,655 public MCP servers leaked in every language studied.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 Fig. 6: leakage >10% per language (Java 19.1% on a small Java denominator, Python 15.4%); §4.2: 192/200 sampled flags confirmed, recall unmeasured; case 2 counts intended API-key use, so the leak definition is broad (review).
relative_to: secret scanning / no secrets in logs (OWASP logging guidance)

reason: It extends known secret-hygiene practice to MCP-specific implicit sinks (tool returns, exceptions) and measures them at ecosystem scale. Treat the prevalence figures as an upper bound.
